title: Maintaining Human Verification Capacity under Automation
abstract: arXiv:2609.38459v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Human verification depends on expertise that must be maintained before it is needed. This paper links reliance on automated checks, investment in human checking ability, and performance during an interruption. Better checking lowers the error reduction gained from an extra unit of human skill while the checker works. It can therefore reduce the incentive to preserve independent expertise, even when it lowers the best achievable expected cost of maintenance and errors. In an illustration, a more informative checker raises detection while it works from \hoPowWorkA{} to \hoPowWorkC{} percent, but the organization then keeps no routine practice and detects \hoPowOnsetC{} percent of errors when the checker first fails, against \hoPowOnsetA{} percent with a less informative checker. translated_title: 自动化背景下人类验证能力的维持
translated_abstract: 人类验证依赖于必须在需要之前就加以维持的专业能力。本文将对自动化检查的依赖、对人类检查能力的投入以及检查中断期间的表现联系起来。更好的自动化检查会降低检查器运行期间每增加一单位人类技能所能带来的错误减少量，因此即使它能降低维护与错误的最佳可达期望成本，也可能削弱组织保留独立专业能力的激励。在一个示例中，信息量更大的检查器将其运行期间的错误检出率从 \hoPowWorkA{}% 提升至 \hoPowWorkC{}%，但组织随后不再保持常规练习，当该检查器首次失效时只能检出 \hoPowOnsetC{}% 的错误，而使用信息量较少的检查器时该比例为 \hoPowOnsetA{}%。因此，检出能力要求既关乎当前的水平，也关乎这一水平在新训练生效之前能否得以存续。来自结肠镜检查和航空领域的证据……（摘要原文在此处截断，且原文中的数值为未填充的占位符）
tldr: 本文指出，更强的自动化检查虽能提升运行期错误检出率并降低期望成本，却会削弱组织维持人类独立核验技能的动力，致使自动化失效时检出能力骤降，因此检出要求必须同时保障当前能力及其在新训练生效前的存续。
en_tdlr: Stronger automated checking improves detection and lowers expected costs but erodes the incentive to maintain independent human verification skills, so a detection requirement must safeguard both current capability and its survival until new training takes effect.
